Reports must identify excluded or incomplete records wherever relevant.  For percentage metrics, display the eligible numerator and denominator alongside the calculated percentage. The reporting layer must preserve both AI-generated and human-confirmed values.  7. Reporting must not bypass existing role permissions, document lifecycle restrictions, or deletion controls.  8. actual_fields.reporting_window: Q7 — REPORTING WINDOW AND CALCULATION RULES  1. DEFAULT REPORTING WINDOW  The first release will use the following reporting periods:  - Default: Last 30 days. - Additional predefined periods: Last 7 days and Last 90 days. - Custom date range: Permitted.  All reporting periods must use explicitly defined start and end boundaries.  The reporting timezone must be consistently applied and clearly identified. Synthetic event timestamps must be generated explicitly and must not be presented as actual production event times.  The default reporting period is a presentation and filtering choice; it does not imply that underlying records may be retained beyond their authorized retention period.  2. PERMITTED REPORTING FILTERS  The first release may support the following filters:  - Tenant. - Reporting period. - Synthetic scenario. - Record type. - Category. - Priority. - Queue. - Classification status. - Document lifecycle status. - Processing status. - Taxonomy and mapping version.  Filter combinations must preserve the underlying metric definitions and eligible-record populations.  All filters and aggregation queries must enforce tenant-scoped authorization.  A user must never be able to access another tenant's data by changing a filter, identifier, or reporting parameter.  3. METRIC-SPECIFIC DATE AND CALCULATION RULES  Each metric must explicitly define its date basis, eligible population, numerator, denominator, and calculation method.  Examples:  - Created Records: Based on SyntheticCreatedAt. - Classification Decisions: Based on the classification decision timestamp. - Human Overrides: Based on the override decision timestamp. - Pending Reviews: Based on the current authorized lifecycle/review state. - Response Time: Based on SyntheticFirstResponseAt minus SyntheticCreatedAt. - Resolution Time: Based on SyntheticResolvedAt minus SyntheticCreatedAt.  A reporting period must use the event timestamp relevant to the metric rather than applying one arbitrary date field to every report.  4. INCLUSION AND EXCLUSION RULES  Only records with valid tenant ownership, identifiable synthetic provenance, and the required metric fields may contribute to the corresponding metric.  Classification metrics must distinguish:  - AI suggestions. - Human-accepted suggestions. - Human-rejected suggestions. - Human overrides. - Pending decisions. - Unassessed decisions.  Completed human classification decisions may contribute to acceptance and override calculations.  Pending, rejected, unassessed, or otherwise ineligible records must not silently be counted as accepted decisions.  Records with invalid or inconsistent timestamps must be excluded from time-based calculations while remaining identifiable in data-quality reporting where authorized.  Deleted or deletion-approved content must not be reintroduced into reporting through retained content or derived data.  All Q1-Q6 lifecycle, validity, deletion, authorization, and retention restrictions remain applicable.  5. MISSING, INVALID AND INCOMPLETE DATA HANDLING  Missing values must never automatically be interpreted as zero.  Use the following reporting representations:  - N/A: Required information is unavailable. - Incomplete: The record lacks one or more required fields. - Invalid: The record contains inconsistent or invalid data. - Pending: The applicable human or processing decision is not complete. - Zero: Use only when the metric was successfully calculated and the actual result is zero.  Reports must identify excluded or incomplete records wherever relevant.  For percentage metrics, display the eligible numerator and denominator alongside the calculated percentage.  If the denominator is zero or unavailable, display N/A rather than zero percent.  If required timestamps are missing, response and resolution metrics must remain unavailable.  No timestamps, missing values, classification decisions, or operational outcomes may be fabricated to complete a report.  6. METRIC DENOMINATORS  Use explicit metric-specific denominators.  Examples:  - Classification Acceptance Rate = Accepted AI Suggestions / Total Completed Eligible Classification Reviews. - Classification Override Rate = Human Overrides / Total Completed Eligible Classification Reviews. - Human Review Pending Count = Number of records currently awaiting the applicable human decision. - Response Time = Valid Synthetic First Response Timestamp minus Valid Synthetic Creation Timestamp. - Resolution Time = Valid Synthetic Resolution Timestamp minus Valid Synthetic Creation Timestamp.  Rejected suggestions must be distinguished from overrides.  A human override must not be counted as an accepted AI suggestion.  The reporting layer must preserve both AI-generated and human-confirmed values.  7. TENANT ISOLATION AND DATA ACCESS  All reports, aggregations, filters, and calculations must enforce tenant-level access controls. Reporting must not bypass existing role permissions, document lifecycle restrictions, or deletion controls.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release adopts a 30-day default reporting window, with 7-day, 90-day, and custom-period options. Tenant isolation, synthetic-data provenance, lifecycle restrictions, and existing Q1-Q6 security and retention decisions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify reporting and calculation requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, establish production SLAs, or permit external data access.
actual_fields.time_semantics: Q7 — CALENDAR, TIMEZONE AND TIMESTAMP SEMANTICS  1. UTC STORAGE AND DISPLAY TIMEZONE  All actual application event timestamps must be stored in UTC.  The first release will use Asia/Kolkata (IST) as the default reporting and display timezone.  Timestamp conversion must happen at the presentation/reporting boundary without changing the underlying stored UTC value.  Synthetic fixture timestamps must also have an explicitly defined timezone or UTC offset and must be normalized consistently for calculations.  The reporting timezone must be clearly identified in reports.  Future tenant-specific timezone configuration remains a separate capability requiring explicit authorization and requirements.  2. ELAPSED-TIME CALCULATION  The first release will use elapsed-time calculations for illustrative synthetic response and resolution metrics.  Elapsed time is the actual difference between two valid event timestamps, independent of working days, weekends, office hours, or holidays.  Business-hours-based calculations are deferred.  The first release does not introduce office calendars, working-day schedules, holiday calendars, business-hour pauses, or production SLA commitments.  3. EVENT TIMESTAMP DEFINITIONS  The following event definitions apply:  A. REQUEST CREATED  The creation timestamp represents the recorded creation event of a request within the application.  For synthetic scenarios, SyntheticCreatedAt represents an explicitly generated fixture event.  For actual application events, the authoritative creation timestamp must come from the recorded application event, not an invented or backdated value.  B. FIRST RESPONSE  The first-response timestamp represents the first recorded, authorized human response event associated with the request.  AI-generated suggestions, automated processing events, system acknowledgements, and unapproved messages must not count as a human first response.  C. RESOLUTION  The resolution timestamp represents the recorded event when an authorized human marks the request as resolved within the application.  AI recommendations or processing completion alone must not constitute resolution.  4. SYNTHETIC FIXTURE VERSUS ACTUAL APPLICATION TIMESTAMPS  Synthetic fixture timestamps and actual application event timestamps must remain distinguishable.  Every timestamp used in reporting must have identifiable provenance, including:  - Event source. - Synthetic or actual event classification. - Associated record and event reference. - Timestamp value. - Applicable timezone or UTC offset. - Event type.  Synthetic fixture timestamps may be used only for illustrative scenario calculations.  They must never be represented as actual customer activity or production operational events.  Actual application timestamps must reflect recorded application events and must not be replaced by generated synthetic values.  Mixing synthetic and actual events in the same metric calculation is prohibited unless a separately approved reporting definition explicitly permits it.  5. REOPENED REQUESTS  A reopened request must generate a separate, auditable Reopened event.  The original creation, first-response, and resolution timestamps must remain preserved.  The first release may report: - Reopened request count. - Reopen event count. - Current request lifecycle status. - Original resolution event reference.  Advanced reopened-request metrics, cumulative resolution calculations, repeated resolution-cycle analytics, and reopen-based SLA calculations are deferred.  A reopened request must not silently overwrite its original resolution history.  6. TIMESTAMP VALIDATION AND DATA QUALITY  All event timestamps must be validated.  The system must identify: - Missing timestamps. - Invalid timestamp values. - Inconsistent event ordering. - Duplicate event records. - Unsupported synthetic/actual provenance.  For example, a first-response timestamp earlier than the corresponding creation timestamp must be treated as invalid for elapsed-time calculations.  Missing or invalid timestamps must produce N/A or an appropriate data-quality status, never an invented duration or zero value.  Original event timestamps must remain auditable.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED CALENDAR AND SLA CAPABILITIES  The following are outside the first-release scope:  - Business-hours-based response and resolution calculations. - Working-day and weekend calendars. - Public holiday calendars. - Tenant-specific operating schedules. - Timezone-specific business calendars. - SLA pause and resume rules. - Business-hours-based SLA breach calculations. - Advanced reopened-request resolution metrics. - Production SLA commitments and compliance reporting.  These capabilities require separately defined requirements, calculation rules, and approval before implementation.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release will store timestamps in UTC and display reporting timestamps in Asia/Kolkata (IST) by default.  Illustrative response and resolution measurements will use elapsed-time calculations based on explicitly recorded or generated synthetic events.  Creation, first response, resolution, and reopening must remain distinct event types with preserved timestamps and identifiable provenance.  Synthetic fixture timestamps must never be presented as actual application events.  Business calendars, working hours, holidays, advanced reopening metrics, and production SLA calculations remain explicitly deferred.  All Q1-Q6 security, authorization, tenant isolation, lifecycle, deletion, and retention requirements remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify timestamp and calendar requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, or establish production SLA commitments.

actual_fields.review_access_actions: Q7 — REPORT ACCESS, GOVERNANCE AND ACTION BOUNDARIES  1. PLATFORM ADMIN REPORT ACCESS  Platform Admin access remains restricted to non-content platform metrics. Override rates must use clearly defined denominators and must not treat pending or unassessed records as completed human decisions.  5. METRIC DEFINITIONS AND DATA QUALITY  Every metric must have a documented definition, calculation method, reporting period, and eligible-record denominator.  In particular:  - Classification Acceptance Rate must measure accepted suggestions against completed review decisions. - Classification Override Rate must measure overridden suggestions against completed review decisions. - Pending Review Count must include only records currently awaiting the applicable human decision. - Response Time and Resolution Time must use valid corresponding event timestamps. - Missing, incomplete, or inconsistent data must be reported as unavailable or excluded according to the documented metric definition.  No unsupported confidence scores, fabricated timestamps, assumed business outcomes, or unverified performance measurements are permitted.  6. REPORTING FILTERS AND TENANT ISOLATION  Reports should support authorized filtering by:  - Tenant. - Reporting period. - Synthetic scenario. - Category. - Priority. - Queue. - Classification status. - Lifecycle status. - Taxonomy/mapping version.  All reporting queries must enforce tenant-scoped authorization.  Platform Admin tenant-content access remains prohibited.  Reports must not expose another tenant's records or restricted document content.  7. SLA AND OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE BOUNDARY  The first release does not establish a production SLA.  Response and resolution time measurements are illustrative synthetic metrics only.  No production response-time commitment, resolution-time target, SLA breach calculation, service availability commitment, or contractual performance claim is implied.  A simulated service policy with defined targets, measurement start events, pause conditions, business calendars, escalation rules, and breach calculations requires a separate explicit decision before implementation.  8. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE DEFERRALS  The following remain deferred:  - Production SLA definitions and commitments. - Real customer and production operational analytics. - Real-world response and resolution performance reporting. - Automated SLA breach detection. - Automatic escalation and notifications. - External ticketing or CRM analytics. - Predictive analytics and AI performance scoring. - Advanced forecasting and trend prediction. - Custom tenant-specific reporting definitions. - Long-term content-bearing analytics history.  9. FINAL DECISION  The first release will deliver a synthetic/local-only illustrative analytics and reporting capability.  It will demonstrate category, priority, classification, override, queue, processing, and lifecycle reporting.  Synthetic response and resolution time measurements are permitted only when supported by explicitly generated synthetic event data and must be labelled accordingly.  AI suggestions and human-confirmed values must remain distinct in all reports.  No real customer data, production SLA, external integration, or unauthorized operational action is introduced.  All Q1-Q6 governance, authorization, tenant isolation, lifecycle, deletion, and retention restrictions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify Q7 reporting scope only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, or establish production service commitments.,

reporting_window.exact_rendered_segment: Q7 — REPORTING WINDOW AND CALCULATION RULES  1. DEFAULT REPORTING WINDOW  The first release will use the following reporting periods:  - Default: Last 30 days. - Additional predefined periods: Last 7 days and Last 90 days. - Custom date range: Permitted.  All reporting periods must use explicitly defined start and end boundaries.  The reporting timezone must be consistently applied and clearly identified. Synthetic event timestamps must be generated explicitly and must not be presented as actual production event times.  The default reporting period is a presentation and filtering choice; it does not imply that underlying records may be retained beyond their authorized retention period.  2. PERMITTED REPORTING FILTERS  The first release may support the following filters:  - Tenant. - Reporting period. - Synthetic scenario. - Record type. - Category. - Priority. - Queue. - Classification status. - Document lifecycle status. - Processing status. - Taxonomy and mapping version.  Filter combinations must preserve the underlying metric definitions and eligible-record populations.  All filters and aggregation queries must enforce tenant-scoped authorization.  A user must never be able to access another tenant's data by changing a filter, identifier, or reporting parameter.  3. METRIC-SPECIFIC DATE AND CALCULATION RULES  Each metric must explicitly define its date basis, eligible population, numerator, denominator, and calculation method.  Examples:  - Created Records: Based on SyntheticCreatedAt. - Classification Decisions: Based on the classification decision timestamp. - Human Overrides: Based on the override decision timestamp. - Pending Reviews: Based on the current authorized lifecycle/review state. - Response Time: Based on SyntheticFirstResponseAt minus SyntheticCreatedAt. - Resolution Time: Based on SyntheticResolvedAt minus SyntheticCreatedAt.  A reporting period must use the event timestamp relevant to the metric rather than applying one arbitrary date field to every report.  4. INCLUSION AND EXCLUSION RULES  Only records with valid tenant ownership, identifiable synthetic provenance, and the required metric fields may contribute to the corresponding metric.  Classification metrics must distinguish:  - AI suggestions. - Human-accepted suggestions. - Human-rejected suggestions. - Human overrides. - Pending decisions. - Unassessed decisions.  Completed human classification decisions may contribute to acceptance and override calculations.  Pending, rejected, unassessed, or otherwise ineligible records must not silently be counted as accepted decisions.  Records with invalid or inconsistent timestamps must be excluded from time-based calculations while remaining identifiable in data-quality reporting where authorized.  Deleted or deletion-approved content must not be reintroduced into reporting through retained content or derived data.  All Q1-Q6 lifecycle, validity, deletion, authorization, and retention restrictions remain applicable.  5. MISSING, INVALID AND INCOMPLETE DATA HANDLING  Missing values must never automatically be interpreted as zero.  Use the following reporting representations:  - N/A: Required information is unavailable. - Incomplete: The record lacks one or more required fields. - Invalid: The record contains inconsistent or invalid data. - Pending: The applicable human or processing decision is not complete. - Zero: Use only when the metric was successfully calculated and the actual result is zero.  Reports must identify excluded or incomplete records wherever relevant.  For percentage metrics, display the eligible numerator and denominator alongside the calculated percentage.  If the denominator is zero or unavailable, display N/A rather than zero percent.  If required timestamps are missing, response and resolution metrics must remain unavailable.  No timestamps, missing values, classification decisions, or operational outcomes may be fabricated to complete a report.  6. METRIC DENOMINATORS  Use explicit metric-specific denominators.  Examples:  - Classification Acceptance Rate = Accepted AI Suggestions / Total Completed Eligible Classification Reviews. - Classification Override Rate = Human Overrides / Total Completed Eligible Classification Reviews. - Human Review Pending Count = Number of records currently awaiting the applicable human decision. - Response Time = Valid Synthetic First Response Timestamp minus Valid Synthetic Creation Timestamp. - Resolution Time = Valid Synthetic Resolution Timestamp minus Valid Synthetic Creation Timestamp.  Rejected suggestions must be distinguished from overrides.  A human override must not be counted as an accepted AI suggestion.  The reporting layer must preserve both AI-generated and human-confirmed values.  7. TENANT ISOLATION AND DATA ACCESS  All reports, aggregations, filters, and calculations must enforce tenant-level access controls.  Tenant identity must be derived from the authenticated and authorized execution context, not blindly trusted from user-supplied filter values.  Cross-tenant aggregation is not permitted in the first release unless separately authorized by an explicit future requirement.  Platform Admin tenant-content access remains prohibited.  Reporting must not bypass existing role permissions, document lifecycle restrictions, or deletion controls.  8. DATA QUALITY AND REPORT TRANSPARENCY  Each report must make its reporting period, applicable filters, metric definitions, eligible-record count, and relevant exclusions understandable to the user.  Synthetic data must be visibly labelled as synthetic.  Unavailable or incomplete information must not be hidden in a way that makes a report appear complete.  Metric calculations must be deterministic and reproducible using the same eligible dataset, reporting boundaries, and calculation rules.  9. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED METRICS  The following remain outside the first-release reporting scope:  - Predictive analytics and forecasting. - Statistical confidence and predictive accuracy scoring. - Production SLA compliance. - Real-world operational performance. - Advanced trend and anomaly detection. - Cross-tenant analytics. - Advanced business-calendar and holiday calculations. - Complex SLA pause, resume, and breach calculations. - Custom tenant-specific metric definitions.  Any future introduction of these metrics requires separately defined requirements, calculation rules, authorization, and approval.  10. FINAL DECISION  The first release adopts a 30-day default reporting window, with 7-day, 90-day, and custom-period options.  Reporting calculations must use explicitly defined event timestamps, metric-specific eligible populations, and transparent denominators.  Missing, invalid, and incomplete data must be represented accurately without treating unavailable values as zero or silently omitting them.  Tenant isolation, synthetic-data provenance, lifecycle restrictions, and existing Q1-Q6 security and retention decisions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify reporting and calculation requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, establish production SLAs, or permit external data access.,

time_semantics.exact_rendered_segment: Q7 — CALENDAR, TIMEZONE AND TIMESTAMP SEMANTICS  1. UTC STORAGE AND DISPLAY TIMEZONE  All actual application event timestamps must be stored in UTC.  The first release will use Asia/Kolkata (IST) as the default reporting and display timezone.  Timestamp conversion must happen at the presentation/reporting boundary without changing the underlying stored UTC value.  Synthetic fixture timestamps must also have an explicitly defined timezone or UTC offset and must be normalized consistently for calculations.  The reporting timezone must be clearly identified in reports.  Future tenant-specific timezone configuration remains a separate capability requiring explicit authorization and requirements.  2. ELAPSED-TIME CALCULATION  The first release will use elapsed-time calculations for illustrative synthetic response and resolution metrics.  Elapsed time is the actual difference between two valid event timestamps, independent of working days, weekends, office hours, or holidays.  Business-hours-based calculations are deferred.  The first release does not introduce office calendars, working-day schedules, holiday calendars, business-hour pauses, or production SLA commitments.  3. EVENT TIMESTAMP DEFINITIONS  The following event definitions apply:  A. REQUEST CREATED  The creation timestamp represents the recorded creation event of a request within the application.  For synthetic scenarios, SyntheticCreatedAt represents an explicitly generated fixture event.  For actual application events, the authoritative creation timestamp must come from the recorded application event, not an invented or backdated value.  B. FIRST RESPONSE  The first-response timestamp represents the first recorded, authorized human response event associated with the request.  AI-generated suggestions, automated processing events, system acknowledgements, and unapproved messages must not count as a human first response.  C. RESOLUTION  The resolution timestamp represents the recorded event when an authorized human marks the request as resolved within the application.  AI recommendations or processing completion alone must not constitute resolution.  4. SYNTHETIC FIXTURE VERSUS ACTUAL APPLICATION TIMESTAMPS  Synthetic fixture timestamps and actual application event timestamps must remain distinguishable.  Every timestamp used in reporting must have identifiable provenance, including:  - Event source. - Synthetic or actual event classification. - Associated record and event reference. - Timestamp value. - Applicable timezone or UTC offset. - Event type.  Synthetic fixture timestamps may be used only for illustrative scenario calculations.  They must never be represented as actual customer activity or production operational events.  Actual application timestamps must reflect recorded application events and must not be replaced by generated synthetic values.  Mixing synthetic and actual events in the same metric calculation is prohibited unless a separately approved reporting definition explicitly permits it.  5. REOPENED REQUESTS  A reopened request must generate a separate, auditable Reopened event.  The original creation, first-response, and resolution timestamps must remain preserved.  The first release may report: - Reopened request count. - Reopen event count. - Current request lifecycle status. - Original resolution event reference.  Advanced reopened-request metrics, cumulative resolution calculations, repeated resolution-cycle analytics, and reopen-based SLA calculations are deferred.  A reopened request must not silently overwrite its original resolution history.  6. TIMESTAMP VALIDATION AND DATA QUALITY  All event timestamps must be validated.  The system must identify: - Missing timestamps. - Invalid timestamp values. - Inconsistent event ordering. - Duplicate event records. - Unsupported synthetic/actual provenance.  For example, a first-response timestamp earlier than the corresponding creation timestamp must be treated as invalid for elapsed-time calculations.  Missing or invalid timestamps must produce N/A or an appropriate data-quality status, never an invented duration or zero value.  Original event timestamps must remain auditable.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED CALENDAR AND SLA CAPABILITIES  The following are outside the first-release scope:  - Business-hours-based response and resolution calculations. - Working-day and weekend calendars. - Public holiday calendars. - Tenant-specific operating schedules. - Timezone-specific business calendars. - SLA pause and resume rules. - Business-hours-based SLA breach calculations. - Advanced reopened-request resolution metrics. - Production SLA commitments and compliance reporting.  These capabilities require separately defined requirements, calculation rules, and approval before implementation.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release will store timestamps in UTC and display reporting timestamps in Asia/Kolkata (IST) by default.  Illustrative response and resolution measurements will use elapsed-time calculations based on explicitly recorded or generated synthetic events.  Creation, first response, resolution, and reopening must remain distinct event types with preserved timestamps and identifiable provenance.  Synthetic fixture timestamps must never be presented as actual application events.  Business calendars, working hours, holidays, advanced reopening metrics, and production SLA calculations remain explicitly deferred.  All Q1-Q6 security, authorization, tenant isolation, lifecycle, deletion, and retention requirements remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify timestamp and calendar requirements only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, or establish production SLA commitments.,

sla_policy.exact_rendered_segment: Q7 — ILLUSTRATIVE INDICATORS, NOT A SIMULATED SLA POLICY  1. FIRST-RELEASE DECISION  Choose illustrative sample indicators clearly labelled as NON-CONTRACTUAL.  The first release will not implement a simulated service-level policy or establish any production SLA commitments.  The purpose is to demonstrate analytics, reporting, and time-based measurement using synthetic/local-only data without creating implied service obligations.  2. PERMITTED ILLUSTRATIVE INDICATORS  The first release may display:  - Average Response Time. - Average Resolution Time. - Fastest Recorded Response. - Longest Recorded Resolution. - Pending Request Count. - Reopened Request Count. - Response and Resolution Time Distribution.  All time-based indicators must be calculated only from valid, explicitly recorded synthetic event timestamps.  These are descriptive measurements, not service targets or commitments.  3. NO SLA TARGETS OR BREACH CALCULATIONS  The first release must not define:  - Priority-based response-time targets. - Priority-based resolution-time targets. - SLA compliance percentages. - SLA breach thresholds. - SLA countdown timers. - SLA warning or breach notifications. - Contractual service availability commitments.  P1 and P2 priority classifications alone must not imply any response or resolution SLA.  4. PRIORITY AND UNASSESSED HANDLING  P1, P2, P3, and P4 may be used to group and compare illustrative time-based metrics.  UNASSESSED records must remain separately identified and must not be assigned an assumed SLA target.  Priority classification must not automatically trigger escalation, notifications, or operational actions.  5. MISSING DATA AND REOPENED REQUESTS  Missing or invalid creation, first-response, or resolution timestamps must result in N/A or an appropriate data-quality status.  Missing values must not be interpreted as zero or treated as successful performance.  Reopened requests must retain their original resolution event and be identified separately.  Advanced cumulative resolution-time calculations and repeated resolution-cycle SLA measurements remain deferred.  6. REPORTING LABELS AND TRANSPARENCY  All relevant dashboards, charts, exports, and reports must clearly display:  "ILLUSTRATIVE — SYNTHETIC DATA — NON-CONTRACTUAL"  Users must be able to distinguish synthetic sample measurements from actual application event measurements.  No indicator may be represented as actual SLA performance, compliance, breach, or contractual service delivery.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED SLA CAPABILITIES  The following require a separate future decision:  - Priority-specific SLA targets. - Business-hours-based SLA calculations. - Working-day and holiday calendars. - SLA pause and resume conditions. - Exact breach boundaries. - Warning and escalation thresholds. - Reopened-request SLA treatment. - SLA compliance reporting. - Production service commitments and operational monitoring.  These deferred capabilities must not be implicitly activated by priority labels or illustrative metrics.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release will provide illustrative, non-contractual response-time and resolution-time indicators using synthetic/local-only data.  No simulated SLA policy, priority-based service target, breach calculation, or production SLA commitment will be introduced.  All Q1-Q6 security, lifecycle, authorization, tenant-isolation, and retention restrictions remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify the first-release analytics boundary only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, or establish any operational or contractual service commitment.,

review_access_actions.exact_rendered_segment: Q7 — REPORT ACCESS, GOVERNANCE AND ACTION BOUNDARIES  1. TENANT-SCOPED REPORT ACCESS  Report access must be controlled through explicitly assigned tenant-scoped permissions.  The first-release access model is:  A. TENANT ADMIN - May view authorized reports for their own tenant. - Must not automatically receive unrestricted document-content or classification-evidence access. - Cannot approve metric definitions merely through administrative status.  B. SUPPORT MANAGER - May view authorized operational reports for their own tenant. - May review support, queue, classification, priority, and pending-review metrics within their assigned scope. - Cannot independently approve central metric or taxonomy definitions.  C. SUPPORT AGENT - May view explicitly authorized, limited support and synthetic-ticket reports within their tenant. - Must not access restricted knowledge content or administrative analytics.  D. KNOWLEDGE REVIEWER - May view authorized knowledge processing, document lifecycle, and review-related metrics. - Access to document content remains subject to separate Knowledge Reviewer permissions.  E. CLASSIFICATION REVIEWER - May view authorized classification, priority, and human-override reports within their tenant. - Cannot modify central metric definitions or taxonomy mappings without separate authority.  2. METRIC AND REPORTING GOVERNANCE  Introduce a separately assigned Analytics Governance Owner permission.  This permission may authorize its holder to propose, review, and approve centrally governed metric definitions and reporting calculation changes within the explicitly assigned scope.  The following rules apply:  - Proposing and approving a material metric change must be separate responsibilities. - A person must not approve their own restricted proposal. - Changes must be version-controlled and auditable. - Effective dates must be explicit. - Existing historical reports must retain their original metric-definition context. - Material changes must not silently rewrite historical results. - Tenant-specific metric customization is outside the first-release scope.  Since the first release does not establish a simulated or production SLA policy, approval of future SLA definitions remains a separate decision and authorization gate.  3. PLATFORM ADMIN REPORT ACCESS  Platform Admin access remains restricted to non-content platform metrics.  Permitted platform-level indicators may include: - Overall synthetic processing health. - Application-level processing status counts. - Non-content technical error counts. - Platform service health indicators. - Aggregate synthetic workload measurements.  Platform Admins must not receive: - Tenant document contents. - Extracted document text. - Knowledge-base content. - Tenant-specific classification evidence. - Content-bearing interaction history. - Restricted tenant analytics that expose protected content.  Platform administration must not imply tenant-content access or Knowledge Reviewer authority.  All access must remain within explicitly authorized platform-level operational boundaries.  4. DASHBOARD RECOMMENDATIONS AND ACTION BOUNDARIES  Analytics indicators and recommendations are informational and advisory.  The first release may display recommendations such as: - Increased pending-review counts. - Increased classification overrides. - High synthetic queue volumes. - Unusual processing failure counts. - Synthetic response and resolution time observations.  However, displaying a recommendation must not automatically: - Escalate a ticket. - Change ticket priority. - Assign or reassign a ticket. - Change a queue. - Send an outgoing message or notification. - Modify external CRM or ticketing records. - Trigger external workflows. - Approve or reject knowledge content. - Change document lifecycle status.  Any future operational action requires a separately authorized workflow and explicit human decision.  5. CONTENT-FREE AUDIT VERSUS RETAINED ANALYTICS DATA  The existing Q5 content-free audit policy remains unchanged.  Content-free audit metadata, including authorized user actions, permission changes, approval decisions, and security events, remains subject to the established 365-day retention requirement.  Analytics data is a separate data category.  The existence of an analytics report or aggregate metric must not automatically authorize additional retention of source documents, extracted text, content-bearing interaction history, or restricted classification evidence.  The following analytics retention details require separate explicit decisions: - Permitted analytics data fields. - Retention duration for synthetic reporting records. - Retention duration for any future actual application metrics. - Aggregation and anonymization requirements. - Deletion propagation requirements. - Access and export permissions.  Synthetic data must remain identifiable as synthetic and must not be mixed with actual customer data without a separately approved requirement.  6. AUDIT AND GOVERNANCE REQUIREMENTS  All report access and governance actions must be auditable.  Record: - User identity. - Tenant or platform scope. - Assigned role and permission. - Report or metric definition accessed or changed. - Action performed. - Timestamp. - Previous and new metric-definition versions, where applicable. - Approval and justification evidence.  Audit records must remain content-free where required by Q5.  Report exports must enforce the same authorization and tenant-isolation rules as on-screen reports.  7. EXPLICIT FIRST-RELEASE DEFERRALS  The following remain deferred:  - Advanced tenant-specific report customization. - Cross-tenant business analytics. - Production SLA definition approval. - SLA policy governance and breach authorization. - Automated recommendations leading to operational actions. - Automated escalation and notifications. - External reporting integrations. - Advanced analytics-data retention policies. - Content-bearing analytics and interaction history. - Advanced report export and sharing permissions.  No deferred capability may be treated as implicitly authorized.  8. FINAL DECISION  The first release will provide tenant-scoped, role-authorized illustrative analytics.  Metric-definition governance will remain separate from ordinary report viewing and administrative account management.  Platform Admin access will remain restricted to non-content platform metrics.  Dashboard recommendations will remain informational and will not trigger automatic ticket changes, escalation, outgoing messages, or external workflows.  The existing Q1-Q6 security, tenant isolation, authorization, lifecycle, deletion, and retention requirements remain unchanged.  These decisions clarify reporting governance and access boundaries only. They do not approve the PRD, authorize implementation, establish production SLA commitments, or permit external actions.,

rationale_deferrals.exact_rendered_segment: Q7 — RATIONALE AND EXPLICIT REMAINING DEFERRALS  1. FIRST-RELEASE DEMONSTRATION OBJECTIVES  The primary objective of the first release is to demonstrate the SupportIQ analytics, reporting, classification, and operational visibility capabilities using synthetic/local-only data.  The first release is intended to validate the reporting experience, metric calculation approach, tenant-scoped access controls, human-reviewed classification, and governance boundaries.  It is not intended to establish production service commitments, contractual SLA obligations, or automated operational decision-making.  2. FIRST-RELEASE METRICS  The first release may demonstrate the following illustrative indicators:  - Category distribution. - Priority distribution. - Average response time. - Average resolution time. - Pending request counts. - Reopened request counts. - Human classification override counts. - Queue and escalation suggestions. - Synthetic processing statistics. - Illustrative request lifecycle distributions.  All metrics must use valid, traceable synthetic/local-only data and the previously established timestamp and calculation rules.  All relevant reports must clearly identify their synthetic and non-contractual nature.  3. NUMERIC TARGETS AND SLA DEFERRALS  No production SLA targets or contractual performance thresholds will be established in the first release.  The following remain explicitly deferred:  - Priority-specific response-time targets. - Priority-specific resolution-time targets. - SLA compliance percentages. - SLA breach thresholds. - SLA countdown and warning indicators. - Production availability and service-performance guarantees. - Automated SLA escalation policies.  P1/P2 classification must not independently imply an SLA commitment.  Undefined numeric targets must remain unavailable rather than being invented or presented as approved policy.  4. CALENDAR AND TIME CALCULATION DEFERRALS  The first release will use UTC event storage, Asia/Kolkata (IST) reporting display, and elapsed-time calculations as previously decided.  The following remain deferred:  - Business-hours calculations. - Working-day calendars. - Weekend and public-holiday exclusions. - Tenant-specific operating calendars. - SLA pause and resume rules. - Business-hours-based breach calculations.  No business calendar or working-hours assumption may be silently introduced.  5. RETENTION AND COMPLIANCE DEFERRALS  The existing Q1-Q6 lifecycle, approval, deletion, audit, and retention decisions remain unchanged.  The following additional analytics-related decisions remain deferred:  - Long-term retention of analytics datasets. - Retention of content-bearing analytics history. - Advanced aggregation and anonymization policies. - Actual customer-data analytics retention. - Additional reporting-data deletion requirements.  The established Q5 retention obligations, including the applicable 24-hour purge, 30-day encrypted-backup age-out, and 365-day content-free audit retention, must not be weakened or bypassed.  A retention deferral does not authorize indefinite retention or override existing deletion requirements.  6. OPERATIONAL AND INTEGRATION DEFERRALS  The first release will not introduce:  - Automatic ticket escalation. - Automatic ticket assignment or reassignment. - Automatic priority changes. - Outgoing customer messages or notifications. - External CRM or ticketing-system writebacks. - Automated workflow execution. - Production SLA monitoring. - Cross-tenant business analytics.  Dashboard recommendations remain informational and require separate human authorization before any future operational action.  7. DATA QUALITY AND UNDEFINED METRICS  Metrics must be calculated only when the required source events, timestamps, provenance, and calculation definitions are valid.  Missing, invalid, conflicting, or insufficient data must be explicitly identified as N/A, UNASSESSED, or an appropriate data-quality state.  The system must not: - Invent timestamps. - Treat unavailable values as zero. - Assume missing SLA targets. - Mix synthetic and actual customer events without separate approval. - Present unverified calculations as implemented guarantees.  Any undefined metric or calculation must remain unavailable or explicitly gated until its definition is approved.  8. REASONS FOR THE FIRST-RELEASE BOUNDARY  This scope keeps the first release focused on demonstrating core analytics and reporting capabilities without prematurely introducing operational complexity, contractual obligations, or unsupported assumptions.  It also preserves the previously established separation between:  - AI suggestions and human-confirmed decisions. - Processing status and approval status. - Report visibility and administrative authority. - Platform metrics and tenant content. - Informational recommendations and authorized operational actions. - Synthetic demonstrations and actual application activity.  9. FINAL DECISION  The first release will demonstrate illustrative analytics using synthetic/local-only data, UTC timestamp storage, IST reporting display, and elapsed-time calculations.  It will not establish production SLA targets, business calendars, contractual service commitments, automated escalation, or external operational integrations.  All unresolved retention, compliance, permission, and advanced analytics requirements remain explicit decision gates before their affected capabilities proceed.  All previously established Q1-Q6 security, tenant isolation, lifecycle, authorization, deletion, approval, and retention safeguards remain unchanged.  These decisions record the intended first-release scope and its rationale only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, or permission to start another process.
